title: Theory of Computation
standfirst: Automata, formal languages, computability and the mathematical limits of what a program can do.
resources_note: An IITM email may be required for some of the resources above; any other access request will be strictly rejected.

description_paragraphs: This course introduces the theory of computation, focusing on abstract models of computation to understand the capabilities and limitations of algorithms. It covers fundamental concepts such as formal languages, simulation, reductions, and nondeterminism, and examines what can be computed efficiently, along with trade-offs between resources like time and space.
faculty: Prof. Partha Pratim Das, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, IIT Kharagpur

weeks_text.label: Week 1
weeks_text.text: Introduction to theory of computation; Finite automata and formal models.

weeks_text.label: Week 2
weeks_text.text: Regular languages; Regular expressions; Language representation.

weeks_text.label: Week 3
weeks_text.text: DFA minimization; Pumping lemma; Properties of regular languages.

weeks_text.label: Week 4
weeks_text.text: Context-free languages (CFLs); Grammars and parse trees.

weeks_text.label: Week 6
weeks_text.text: Non-context-free languages; Introduction to Turing machines.

weeks_text.label: Week 7
weeks_text.text: Variants of Turing machines; Church-Turing thesis.

weeks_text.label: Week 10
weeks_text.text: Time and space complexity; Complexity classes.

weeks_text.label: Week 12
weeks_text.text: NP-completeness; Course summary and unifying concepts.
